explanation_en: "Desde o primeiro momento" translates to "from the very first moment" or "right from the start." It is a strong, emphatic way to say "from the beginning" (desde o início). It is highly common in narrative contexts, news reporting, and daily conversations to emphasize that a state or action has been true since the absolute inception of an event.

examples.en_text: From the very beginning, I realized this company was the right place for me.
examples.target_text: Desde o primeiro momento, percebi que esta empresa era o lugar certo para mim.

examples.en_text: They supported our decision from the very beginning.
examples.target_text: Eles apoiaram a nossa decisão desde o primeiro momento.

examples.en_text: We organized everything very well from the very beginning.
examples.target_text: Nós organizamos tudo muito bem desde o primeiro momento.

examples.en_text: From the very beginning, I felt I could trust him.
examples.target_text: Desde o primeiro momento, senti que podia confiar nele.

examples.en_text: She loved the photography course from the very beginning.
examples.target_text: Ela adorou o curso de fotografia desde o primeiro momento.

examples.en_text: I wanted to be honest with you from the very beginning.
examples.target_text: Eu quis ser sincero contigo desde o primeiro momento.

explanation_en: This expression means to pay for something using one's own personal funds rather than relying on an employer, the state, or someone else to cover the cost. It is a very common and useful collocation in both everyday conversations and financial or political discussions.

examples.en_text: Since the company didn't pay for the course, I had to pay for it out of my own pocket.
examples.target_text: Como a empresa não pagou pelo curso, tive que tirar do meu próprio bolso.

examples.en_text: He is paying out of his own pocket to keep the project running.
examples.target_text: Ele está tirando do próprio bolso para manter o projeto funcionando.

examples.en_text: We didn't want to ask for help, so we ended up paying out of our own pocket.
examples.target_text: Nós não queríamos pedir ajuda, então acabamos tirando do nosso próprio bolso.

examples.en_text: If the city hall doesn't help, the organizers will have to pay for everything out of their own pocket.
examples.target_text: Se a prefeitura não ajudar, os organizadores vão ter que tirar tudo do próprio bolso.

examples.en_text: The insurance didn't cover the damage to the car, so she paid for the repair out of her own pocket.
examples.target_text: O seguro não cobriu o estrago do carro, então ela pagou o conserto tirando do próprio bolso.

examples.en_text: Many teachers end up paying out of their own pocket to buy materials for the students.
examples.target_text: Muitos professores acabam tirando do próprio bolso para comprar material para os alunos.

explanation_en: A 'nota de repúdio' is a formal, written public statement issued by an institution, group, or public figure to express strong disapproval, condemnation, or rejection of an action or statement. It is a standard term in Brazilian political, corporate, and journalistic discourse.

examples.en_text: The university published an official statement of condemnation against the acts of vandalism on campus.
examples.target_text: A universidade publicou uma nota de repúdio contra os atos de vandalismo no campus.

examples.en_text: The soccer club issued an official statement of condemnation after the racist insults against the player.
examples.target_text: O clube de futebol emitiu uma nota de repúdio após os insultos racistas contra o jogador.

examples.en_text: The government released an official statement of condemnation criticizing the neighboring country's decision.
examples.target_text: O governo lançou uma nota de repúdio criticando a decisão do país vizinho.

examples.en_text: Several journalists signed an official statement of condemnation against press censorship.
examples.target_text: Vários jornalistas assinaram uma nota de repúdio contra a censura na imprensa.

examples.en_text: The famous actor posted an official statement of condemnation on his social media to defend himself against the accusations.
examples.target_text: O famoso ator publicou uma nota de repúdio em suas redes sociais para se defender das acusações.

examples.en_text: The medical association released an official statement of condemnation regarding the new health measures.
examples.target_text: A associação médica divulgou uma nota de repúdio sobre as novas medidas de saúde.

explanation_en: Derived from the verb phrase 'rasgar seda' (literally 'to tear silk'), 'rasgação de seda' refers to the act of praising someone excessively, often to the point of being sycophantic or insincere. It is a very common colloquial expression in Brazil, used in both personal and professional contexts to describe over-the-top compliments.

examples.en_text: I can't stand seeing João showering the boss with excessive flattery every day.
examples.target_text: Eu não aguento mais ver o João fazendo essa rasgação de seda com o chefe todo dia.

examples.en_text: You really did a great job, and I say this without any insincere flattery.
examples.target_text: Você realmente fez um ótimo trabalho, e digo isso sem nenhuma rasgação de seda.

examples.en_text: His Instagram post was full of mutual flattery in the comments.
examples.target_text: A publicação dele no Instagram estava cheia de rasgação de seda nos comentários.

examples.en_text: When my sister starts with this excessive flattery, I already know she wants to borrow money.
examples.target_text: Quando minha irmã começa com essa rasgação de seda, eu já sei que ela quer pedir dinheiro emprestado.

examples.en_text: Let's get straight to the point and leave the sweet-talking aside, as we are short on time.
examples.target_text: Vamos direto ao ponto e deixar a rasgação de seda de lado, pois temos pouco tempo.

examples.en_text: The interview was a bit boring because it was just mutual flattery between the host and the guest.
examples.target_text: A entrevista foi um pouco chata porque ficou só na rasgação de seda entre o apresentador e o convidado.

explanation_en: This is a very common fixed phrase meaning 'from beginning to end' or 'throughout the entire duration.' It can be used to describe books, movies, events, or behaviors that remain consistent throughout. It is highly versatile and natural.

examples.en_text: I read the book from start to finish in just two days.
examples.target_text: Eu li o livro do começo ao fim em apenas dois dias.

examples.en_text: We organized the event from start to finish without any outside help.
examples.target_text: Nós organizamos o evento do começo ao fim sem nenhuma ajuda externa.

examples.en_text: She told me the whole story, from start to finish, and I was surprised.
examples.target_text: Ela me contou a história toda, do começo ao fim, e eu fiquei surpreso.

examples.en_text: I want to take this cooking course from start to finish to really learn.
examples.target_text: Quero fazer este curso de culinária do começo ao fim para aprender de verdade.

examples.en_text: The team played very well from the start to the finish of the match.
examples.target_text: O time jogou muito bem do começo ao fim da partida.

examples.en_text: He followed the construction of the house from start to finish.
examples.target_text: Ele acompanhou a construção da casa do começo ao fim.

explanation_en: This is a rhetorical set phrase used to express that one does not have the moral authority to criticize or pass judgment on others, usually because they have made similar mistakes in the past. It is the exact equivalent of the English 'who are we to judge.'

examples.en_text: They decided to get married after only a month of dating; but who are we to judge?
examples.target_text: Eles decidiram se casar depois de apenas um mês de namoro; mas quem somos nós para julgar?

examples.en_text: She spends all her money on travel, but who are we to judge what brings happiness to others?
examples.target_text: Ela gasta todo o seu dinheiro em viagens, mas quem somos nós para julgar o que traz felicidade aos outros?

examples.en_text: If they prefer to homeschool their children, who are we to judge their decisions?
examples.target_text: Se eles preferem educar os filhos em casa, quem somos nós para julgar as decisões deles?

examples.en_text: He decided to quit a good job to start his own business. Who are we to judge?
examples.target_text: Ele resolveu largar um bom emprego para abrir o próprio negócio. Quem somos nós para julgar?

examples.en_text: Everyone makes mistakes in life, so who are we to judge someone's past?
examples.target_text: Todo mundo comete erros na vida, então quem somos nós para julgar o passado de alguém?

examples.en_text: They decided to sell everything and live in a van, but who are we to judge their lifestyle?
examples.target_text: Eles decidiram vender tudo e morar em uma van, mas quem somos nós para julgar o estilo de vida deles?

explanation_en: 'Se ferrar' is a very common colloquial, slightly slangy verb phrase that means to get into deep trouble, to fail miserably, or to get screwed over. While not vulgar, it is informal and should be avoided in formal writing, though it is extremely common in spoken Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.en_text: I didn't study at all for the math exam and I got screwed.
examples.target_text: Eu não estudei nada para a prova de matemática e me ferrei.

examples.en_text: He tried to save money by buying a very cheap used car and got screwed.
examples.target_text: Ele tentou economizar comprando um carro usado muito barato e se ferrou.

examples.en_text: If you keep arriving late to work, you'll end up getting screwed.
examples.target_text: Se você continuar chegando atrasado no trabalho, vai acabar se ferrando.

examples.en_text: We forgot to check the weather forecast and got screwed by the rain.
examples.target_text: Nós esquecemos de olhar a previsão do tempo e nos ferramos com a chuva.

examples.en_text: They left buying the tickets to the last minute and got screwed because they sold out.
examples.target_text: Eles deixaram para comprar os ingressos na última hora e se ferraram porque esgotou.

examples.en_text: I hope he doesn't get screwed by this hasty decision.
examples.target_text: Espero que ele não se ferre com essa decisão apressada.

explanation_en: 'Pau mandado' is an informal, derogatory expression used to describe someone who blindly obeys orders from another person, acting as a puppet or lackey. It carries a strong connotation of weakness and lack of autonomy. Learners should use it carefully as it is highly informal and insulting.

examples.en_text: He doesn't make any decisions on his own; he's just the boss's lackey.
examples.target_text: Ele não toma nenhuma decisão sozinho; é só um pau mandado do chefe.

examples.en_text: My brother does everything his girlfriend wants; he has become a real puppet.
examples.target_text: O meu irmão faz tudo o que a namorada quer, ele virou um verdadeiro pau mandado.

examples.en_text: The new director has no power at all; he is just a puppet of the company owners.
examples.target_text: O novo diretor não tem poder nenhum, ele é apenas um pau mandado dos donos da empresa.

examples.en_text: I'm not going to do what he wants; I'm nobody's lackey!
examples.target_text: Eu não vou fazer o que ele quer; não sou pau mandado de ninguém!

examples.en_text: You need to learn to say no and stop being your cousin's yes-man.
examples.target_text: Você precisa aprender a dizer não e deixar de ser o pau mandado do seu primo.

examples.en_text: In the work group, Pedro does all the boring work because he is the others' lackey.
examples.target_text: No grupo de trabalho, o Pedro faz todo o serviço chato porque é um pau mandado dos outros.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to give something to someone easily, without them having to make any effort to obtain it. It is equivalent to the English 'on a silver platter' or 'handed to someone.' It is widely used in everyday Portuguese and is highly natural.

examples.en_text: He thinks he is going to get the job on a silver platter just because he is the owner's son.
examples.target_text: Ele acha que vai conseguir o emprego de mão beijada só porque é filho do dono.

examples.en_text: We made a lot of mistakes and handed the victory to the opponent on a silver platter.
examples.target_text: Nós cometemos muitos erros e entregamos a vitória ao adversário de mão beijada.

examples.en_text: She didn't have to work to buy the apartment; she got it on a silver platter from her parents.
examples.target_text: Ela não teve que trabalhar para comprar o apartamento; ganhou de mão beijada dos pais.

examples.en_text: The teacher is not going to give you the test answers on a silver platter; you need to study.
examples.target_text: O professor não vai te dar as respostas do teste de mão beijada; você precisa estudar.

examples.en_text: We can't accept this proposal right from the start, or they will think they got the contract on a silver platter.
examples.target_text: Não podemos aceitar essa proposta logo de início, ou eles vão achar que levaram o contrato de mão beijada.

examples.en_text: In life, nothing comes on a silver platter; everything requires effort and dedication.
examples.target_text: Na vida, nada vem de mão beijada; tudo exige esforço e dedicação.

explanation_en: Literally 'to go up the ramp,' this expression refers specifically to the architectural ramp of the Palácio do Planalto in Brasília, which the president-elect climbs during the inauguration ceremony. Idiomatically, it means to assume the presidency or take high executive office in Brazil. It is a highly specific political idiom.

examples.en_text: The new president will take office at the Planalto Palace on January first.
examples.target_text: O novo presidente vai subir a rampa do Palácio do Planalto no dia primeiro de janeiro.

examples.en_text: I remember the day she took office and made that emotional speech.
examples.target_text: Eu me lembro do dia em que ela subiu a rampa e fez aquele discurso emocionante.

examples.en_text: Many political analysts doubt that he will take office after the elections.
examples.target_text: Muitos analistas políticos duvidam que ele vá subir a rampa após as eleições.

examples.en_text: Whoever wins Sunday's election will have the honor of taking presidential office.
examples.target_text: Quem vencer a eleição de domingo terá a honra de subir a rampa presidencial.

examples.en_text: All the international press was present to see the president-elect take office.
examples.target_text: Toda a imprensa internacional estava presente para ver o presidente eleito subir a rampa.

examples.en_text: He won the election, but because of the protests, he almost didn't manage to take office.
examples.target_text: Ele ganhou a eleição, mas por causa dos protestos, quase não conseguiu subir a rampa.

explanation_en: 'Capenga' literally means lame or limping (referring to a person or animal). Figuratively, it is used to describe something that is weak, poorly functioning, incomplete, or unstable, such as an argument, a system, or political support. It is a highly expressive and common B2/C1 word.

examples.en_text: This dining table is a bit shaky, we need to fix its leg.
examples.target_text: Essa mesa de jantar está meio capenga, precisamos consertar o pé dela.

examples.en_text: The excuse he gave for being late was very weak, and nobody believed it.
examples.target_text: A desculpa que ele deu para o atraso foi muito capenga e ninguém acreditou.

examples.en_text: The project started well, but now the organization is a bit shaky.
examples.target_text: O projeto começou bem, mas agora a organização está meio capenga.

examples.en_text: After playing soccer, João was limping for a week.
examples.target_text: Depois de jogar futebol, o João ficou capenga por uma semana.

examples.en_text: With the current crisis, the country's economy remains unstable.
examples.target_text: Com a crise atual, a economia do país continua capenga.

examples.en_text: Our internet connection is super shaky today.
examples.target_text: A nossa conexão de internet está super capenga hoje.

explanation_en: This expression comes from boxing ('to lower one's guard') and is used metaphorically to mean becoming less vigilant, relaxed, or unprepared for potential danger or criticism. It is a very common and useful idiom in both personal and professional contexts.

examples.en_text: Don't lower your guard, the game isn't over yet!
examples.target_text: Não baixem a guarda, o jogo ainda não acabou!

examples.en_text: After talking to him for a few hours, she finally lowered her guard.
examples.target_text: Depois de conversar com ele por algumas horas, ela finalmente baixou a guarda.

examples.en_text: The fighter lowered his guard for a second and ended up losing the fight.
examples.target_text: O lutador baixou a guarda por um segundo e acabou perdendo a luta.

examples.en_text: If we lower our guard, they will find out our secret.
examples.target_text: Se nós baixarmos a guarda, eles vão descobrir o nosso segredo.

examples.en_text: It's hard to make friends when you are afraid of lowering your guard.
examples.target_text: É difícil fazer amigos quando você tem medo de baixar a guarda.

examples.en_text: In that city, you can't lower your guard even for a moment.
examples.target_text: Naquela cidade, você não pode baixar a guarda nem por um momento.
